title: An issue closed long ago, but no release has ever claimed it
author: off-by-one
description: The issue-side twin of merged-pr-never-released (task 381) and milestone-closed-never-released (task 383) -- the third and last leg of the same closed-but-uncredited-by-any-release family, completing the set across all three GitHub record types a release's own body can claim credit for (PR, milestone, issue). Reuses release-claims-unfixed-issue's own real closing-keyword grammar (fixes/closes/resolves #N, both tenses) rather than inventing a fourth claim phrase -- an issue already has a real, canonical GitHub credit phrase. Reads across every release read so far, not just the newest one -- an issue can go uncredited across several releases in a row, so clearing only the newest is not enough.
confidence_notes: Age-gated at 96 hours since the issue's own closed_at, matching merged-pr-never-released's and milestone-closed-never-released's own bar exactly -- the same family, the same reasoning, the third record type. Under 96h scores 0.5 (below the 0.70 bar, weighed in the tail not hidden). At or past 96h scores a flat 0.85. An issue that is still open is excluded at confidence 0.0, named not hidden -- there is nothing for a release to have missed yet. A closed issue that IS claimed by at least one release read so far, at any point in that history, is excluded too -- the claim was kept. A bare '#N' mention with no real closing keyword (e.g. 'see #N for background') never clears the issue -- it is not a credit claim.
